passages.observation: Jesus contrasts the good shepherd with the hired hand, speaks of knowing the sheep, gathering one flock, laying down his life, and taking it again by received command.

passages.title: A council decides that one man should die
passages.excerpt: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, “What are we doing? For this man does many signs.  If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans wi…
passages.observation: Chief priests and Pharisees gather a council; Caiaphas argues that one person should die for the people, the narrator widens the statement, and from that day they plan Jesus’ death.

passages.title: Prayer, sleeping disciples, betrayal, and arrest
passages.excerpt: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”  He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and se…
passages.observation: In Gethsemane Jesus prays three times, the disciples sleep, Judas arrives with an armed crowd and a kiss, a sword is used, and Jesus is seized as the disciples flee.

passages.title: Jesus steps forward; the arresting party falls back
passages.excerpt: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.  Now Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place,…
passages.observation: Jesus enters a garden, meets Judas and an armed party, identifies himself, protects his disciples, stops Peter’s sword, speaks of the cup, and is bound.

passages.observation: Jesus is taken to Caiaphas, witnesses seek testimony, two speakers cite the temple saying, the high priest questions Jesus, and the council declares him worthy of death before abuse begins.

passages.title: Reasoning that the Christ had to suffer
passages.phase: The event named in public proclamation

passages.observation: Paul says Christ’s love constrains because one died for all, speaks of changed regard and new creation, and names reconciliation and entrusted speech.

passages.title: A prepared body and one offering

passages.observation: Hebrews places Psalm words on Christ’s lips, contrasts repeated offerings with doing God’s will, and speaks of one offering, seated completion, and remembered covenant words.

passages.title: Blood outside the gate; reproach outside the camp
passages.phase: The cross in letters and later memory

passages.observation: Hebrews recalls bodies burned outside the camp and says Jesus suffered outside the gate to sanctify people through his blood, then calls hearers to go outside bearing reproach.

passages.title: Redeemed by precious blood, foreknown and revealed

passages.title: Christ suffers once, the righteous for the unrighteous

passages.observation: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins to bring people to God, was put to death in flesh and made alive in spirit, and continues through proclamation, baptism, and exaltation.

passages.title: Love known by a laid-down life

passages.observation: The writer says love is known because Jesus laid down his life, then turns to brothers and sisters, material need, action, truth, and mutual life-giving.
